limits: Static trace only: no captured instruction was executed and no concrete input values were observed.  The direct-access census covers the record registers, the pinned alias registers and the stack bases of the twenty-two pinned bodies, at the embeddings the traced call sites establish; whole-record copies move bytes without naming fields -- the copies observed are enumerated in the call paths (the spawn bodies' struct copies, the wrappers' payload and record copies, the shaping copies of lvl4_a/lvl3_c) -- so for copied fields the census is a statement about direct accesses and the copies actually observed.  The step from the wrappers' heap task records to the lvl3_d/e invocations is established by the relocation slots, the wrappers' slot-address stores and the exact offset alignment (payload byte 0 lands at task record +0x38, the lvl2 record's embedding offset in the lvl3 entry structs); the executor that performs the invocation is not identified.  The phase-struct layout shared by lvl4_a, lvl3_c and ctor_c's frame (dispatch byte +0x21a, shaping at +0x220) is established by identical offsets and store shapes, not by type information.  Jump-table arm reachability is recorded where the earlier packets recorded it and is not re-decided here.  The two registrars and the helper bodies 0x5cf93f0, 0x2d4d540 are censused as call targets only; their bodies are not pinned by this packet.  Raw values are recorded mechanically; no field types are guessed.

a_chain_producer.record_head: lvl3_a is the producer of the lvl2_a record's head: it stores the pair before the record and the record's first 0x22 bytes from its own struct's fields and from an indirect call through GOT slot 0x64e7430 immediately before calling lvl2_a (pins in the lvl3_a owner record)
a_chain_producer.shaping: lvl4_a shapes the sub-struct it passes to lvl3_a out of its phase struct's +0xc8..+0xf0 fields, with the tag byte at +0x248 set to 2 or 1 by arm; those source fields are themselves the phase struct's incoming contents -- lvl4_a's callers are lvl4_c (stack buffer) and call4a_b (a double dereference of its entry rdx)

c_chain_producer.stack_construction: lvl4_c produces every record it hands down on its own stack frame; the phase struct it passes to lvl4_a is filled by an indirect call through GOT slot 0x64e1760 out of the query struct the helper 0x5cf93f0 filled
c_chain_producer.top: ctor_c passes its own stack frame as lvl4_c's phase struct and initialises only its dispatch byte; ctor_c is reachable only through the registration stub 0x2cef8f0 (sole lea reference 0x2cef8f7), which registers it through GOT slot 0x64e6c30 under the key cell 0x6440b48; the stub is the binary's main function, loaded by the ELF entry point at 0x1419318

d_e_chain_producer.forwarders: lvl3_d1/d2/e1/e2 never write the embedded lvl2 record (its only direct reference is the lea forming the call argument); they are invoked through .data.rel.ro cells whose addresses the four wrapper spawners embed at +0x10 of 0x3080-byte heap task records tagged 0xcc
d_e_chain_producer.payload_origin: the 0x2ff8-byte payload that lands at task record +0x38 -- the lvl2 record's embedding offset inside the lvl3 entry structs -- is assembled by spawn_d and spawn_e on their own stacks as the record at [rsp+0x3390] of a 0x3008-byte struct, through the helper calls and copies recorded in their call paths, then copied to [rsp+0x9390] and handed down through pre_d/pre_e and the wrappers; the byte-level writers of the descriptor fields inside the payload are those helper calls, which do not name the offsets in any body in the window
d_e_chain_producer.spawn_reachability: spawn_d and spawn_e are themselves reached only through the handler table slots 0x64478f0/0x64478d0 (no rip-relative reference to either slot), so their invocation is a table walk

descriptor_fields.fields: bulk selector (block +0x178), bulk incoming limit (+0x1b0), twin source pointer (+0x8), twin sibling (+0x108), twin incoming limit (+0x110), as mapped in the input-writers and block-fill packets
